drafts.rationale: The evidence caps how many times Orion may execute a job, as an initial run plus bounded retries. EV-O-A01 and EV-O-A16 both address this same attempt-budget locus.
drafts.subject: Orion job execution

drafts.rationale: The evidence specifies the wait after a failed execution before Orion may deliver the job again. EV-O-B01 and EV-O-B16 both concern this retry-delay policy.
drafts.subject: Orion job retry

drafts.rationale: The evidence bounds how long one execution may run and treats reaching that limit as a failed attempt. EV-O-C01 and EV-O-C16 both describe this timeout locus.
drafts.subject: Orion execution attempt

drafts.rationale: The evidence specifies how further deliveries of an already-active job are ignored or rejected. EV-O-D01 and EV-O-D16 both address this duplicate-delivery locus.
drafts.subject: Orion job delivery

drafts.rationale: The evidence requires Orion to remember each producer idempotency key for a bounded time after it is first seen. EV-O-E01 and EV-O-E16 both address this retention locus.
drafts.subject: Orion idempotency key

drafts.rationale: The evidence grants a worker exclusive ownership of a delivered job for a fixed period and makes the job available to others when that period ends. EV-O-F01 and EV-O-F16 both address lease lifetime.
drafts.subject: Orion worker lease

drafts.rationale: The evidence specifies when a worker may extend a lease while work is progressing and how far a renewal stretches it. EV-O-G01 and EV-O-G16 both address lease renewal.
drafts.subject: Orion worker lease

drafts.rationale: The evidence defines that cancellation bars future attempts without aborting a running attempt, and that a repeated cancel is a no-op. EV-O-H01 and EV-O-H16 both address this cancellation locus.
drafts.subject: Orion job cancellation

drafts.rationale: The evidence specifies what Orion does with a job after its last unsuccessful execution. EV-O-I01 and EV-O-I16 both address this post-exhaustion disposition.
drafts.subject: Orion job

drafts.rationale: The evidence defines when repeated dead-letter events for one tenant must raise an operator escalation. EV-O-J01 and EV-O-J16 both address this escalation-threshold locus.
drafts.subject: Orion operator escalation

drafts.rationale: The evidence guarantees first-in-first-out execution only among jobs in the same partition and none across partitions. EV-O-K01 and EV-O-K16 both address this ordering promise.
drafts.subject: Orion queue execution order

drafts.rationale: The evidence requires job-state audit records to remain available for a bounded period and then allows deletion. EV-O-L01 and EV-O-L16 both address audit retention.
drafts.subject: Orion audit events

drafts.rationale: EV-O-A02 states that a job may be executed at most three times in total and that the first execution counts as one of those three.

value.text: A job must be executed at most three times in total, with the first execution counting as one of the three.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-A16 caps retries at three after the original execution, which is a different budget from a three-execution total.

value.text: One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions; after three unsuccessful retries the job must not be executed again.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-B16 requires a wait of exactly five seconds before every retry, not shortened or lengthened by attempt number.
EV-O-B07 requires a two-second first wait that doubles on later retries and is capped at thirty seconds, which cannot hold together with a fixed five-second wait.

value.text: Wait two seconds before the first retry, then double the wait before each later retry, never exceeding thirty seconds.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-C16 bounds each execution at half a minute and requires the timed-out execution to be stopped and recorded as failed.

value.text: An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped and recorded as a failed attempt.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-D09 ignores every further delivery of an active job id, without using an idempotency key.

value.text: While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored and must not change the active job's state.

drafts.predicate: duplicate handling by job id and idempotency key
drafts.rationale: EV-O-D16 ignores a redelivery only when job id and idempotency key both match, and rejects a same job id with a different key.

value.text: While a job is active, a further delivery is ignored only when it carries both the same job id and the same idempotency key; a same job id with a different key is rejected as conflicting input and must not change the active job's state.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-E16 requires each idempotency key to be retained for twenty-four hours after it is first seen, after which it may be forgotten.
EV-O-F06 requires a worker lease to last sixty seconds from delivery and to make the job available to other workers when that lease expires without renewal or release.
EV-O-F16 states that a worker owns a delivered job for one and a half minutes unless the lease is renewed or released earlier, after which the job becomes available to other workers.
EV-O-G11 allows renewal every thirty seconds during progress and extends the lease by the full duration from renewal.

value.text: A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work is progressing, and a renewal extends the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-G16 replaces a thirty-second optional cadence with a twenty-second remaining-life trigger and a fifteen-second minimum interval.

value.text: A worker must renew when twenty seconds of lease life remain if work is progressing, must never renew the same lease more often than once every fifteen seconds, and a renewal extends the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

drafts.predicate: effect on current and future attempts
drafts.rationale: EV-O-H16 forbids later attempts after cancel, leaves a running attempt to finish, and treats a repeated cancellation as a no-op on job state.

value.text: After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt may be started; a running attempt is not interrupted; a repeated cancellation leaves the job cancelled and must not otherwise change its state.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-I15 requires automatic movement to the dead-letter queue after the last unsuccessful attempt, with no further execution unless resubmitted.

value.text: After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue, and a job there must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-I16 keeps an exhausted job in the failed state for operator review and forbids automatic dead-lettering.

value.text: After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must leave the job in the failed state requiring operator review and must not automatically move it to the dead-letter queue.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-J13 escalates after three dead-letter events for one tenant within one hour from the first event.

value.text: When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour measured from the first of the three events, Orion must raise an operator escalation.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-J16 escalates after five dead-letter events for one tenant in a rolling thirty-minute window, which cannot hold together with a three-in-one-hour rule.

value.text: When five dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within any rolling thirty-minute window, Orion must raise an operator escalation.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-K16 confines the FIFO guarantee to a single queue partition and denies any ordering promise across partitions.

value.text: First-in-first-out execution order is guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition; no ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

drafts.rationale: EV-O-L16 requires audit history to remain queryable for one month, defined as thirty calendar days from recording, after which an event may be deleted.
